Code review: non-atomic HTML file write in FetchCache::put() is acceptable for a local tool; get() gracefully handles orphaned manifest entries by returning null when the HTML file is missing. No bugs found.

comments.note: FetchCache::put() writes the HTML file with file_put_contents() (not atomic) then writes the manifest atomically via JSONFile::putData(). If the process crashes between the two writes, the manifest has an entry pointing to a partially-written or missing HTML file. FetchCache::get() already handles the missing-file case gracefully (returns null), so the cache degrades correctly — no data corruption. Acceptable for a local-only tool; no action required.

FetchCache::get() returns null when the HTML file is missing even if a manifest entry exists, but does not prune that orphaned entry. The entry will linger in the manifest until invalidate() or invalidateAll() is called. Low-risk cosmetic debt.

The $url parameter of FetchCache::get() is accepted but unused in the lookup logic (lookup is purely by $type). The parameter exists for API symmetry with put() and for potential future validation. A docblock clarification would help prevent caller confusion.

Two medium-priority open findings from prior WPs remain unresolved and are forwarded: (1) getCacheFolder() path discrepancy — returns {comicFolder}/cache but cache lives at {comicFolder}/downloaded/cache; (2) put() does not guard the file_put_contents() return value before saveManifest(). Both are carry-over debt items, not regressions introduced by WP-005.

Overall code quality is high. The cache architecture (lazy manifest, atomic manifest writes via JSONFile, clean in-memory → disk → HTTP fallback chain in fetchHTML()) is sound and consistent with project conventions.

comments.note: getCacheFolder() path discrepancy (carry-over from WP-002, still unresolved): Comic::getCacheFolder() returns {getFolder()}/cache, but Fetcher constructs FetchCache with $this->folder = getStorageFolder() = {getFolder()}/downloaded, placing the actual cache at {getFolder()}/downloaded/cache. No current code calls getCacheFolder() for file I/O (Fetcher bypasses it), but the method is a latent trap — any future caller who uses getCacheFolder() to locate cache files will be silently wrong. Fix: change getCacheFolder() to return getStorageFolder().'/cache', or construct FetchCache with $this->comic->getCacheFolder() in the Fetcher constructor.

FetchCache::put() (carry-over from WP-001/WP-002, still unresolved): file_put_contents($htmlFile, $html) return value is not checked before calling saveManifest(). A failed write (disk full, permissions) silently creates a manifest entry pointing to a non-existent or zero-byte HTML file. get() will return null on the next miss, but the stale manifest entry persists. Recommend adding: if(file_put_contents($htmlFile, $html) === false) { throw new WebcomicsBuilderException(..., YYMMNN); } before saveManifest().

FetchCache::get() accepts a $url parameter (string) that is entirely unused in the read path — it is only ever written in put(). The parameter creates API noise and misleads callers. Recommend removing $url from get() and updating all call sites (currently only Fetcher::fetchHTML() line ~123).

FetchCache::isValid() checks only the manifest timestamp, not whether the HTML file exists on disk. This creates a contract asymmetry: isValid() can return true while get() returns null (e.g. if the html/ file was deleted externally). Callers using isValid() as a pre-flight guard before get() will be surprised. Consider adding a file_exists() check in isValid(), or document the asymmetry clearly in the method docblock.

fetchHTML() cache integration (Fetcher.php ~line 110-150): the in-memory → persistent → HTTP fallback chain is clean and correct. bypassCache=true skips only the disk-cache read (step 2), but still writes to the disk cache after the fresh HTTP download (step 4) — this is the correct design for a forced-refresh scenario. Implementation is idiomatic.
